reviewer: outdoor_pool assistant subagent; pool implementation contributor, performing a separate direct inspection of these final rendered captures. This is not blinded external validation.
review_method: All seven original 1152x720 PNGs opened directly with view_image. No image editing, avatar hiding, camera change, runtime source change or engine execution during review. Screenshot impressions are separated from numeric production test observations.

images.name: hotel_pool_normal_arrival
visible: Wide flush water surface is immediately ahead of the actual lift landing.
Deck, coping, glass roof edge and surrounding skyline read as an outdoor rooftop pool.
Original avatar remains in the central opening; the lift doorway posts frame the sides.
Compact roof HUD states E floor selection and roof jump exit; no unrelated street entrance card overlays the pool.
limitations: The near lift prompt overlaps part of the lower legs in this arrival frame.
Loungers, parasols and shower are best seen after turning toward the long axis, rather than all appearing in the initial forward view.

images.name: jump_above_flush_pool
visible: The long swimming rectangle and lane strips are legible at the deck edge, with no raised tank wall blocking the water.
Sun loungers, parasols, shower/towel props, planting, lift enclosure and the open skyline are visible together.
The avatar remains visible above the coping and water during the jump.
limitations: The construction and water shading remain deliberately simple low-poly game assets.

images.name: splash_on_physical_entry
visible: Finite droplets and a surface ring surround the visible torso on physical water entry.
The pool edge is flush with the walkable deck and the far leisure zone remains visible.
Swimming HUD explicitly shows movement controls and Space water exit.
limitations: The entry handrail crosses the lower foreground; it does not obscure the avatar head/torso but occupies a noticeable part of this view.

images.name: buoyant_swimming_in_sunken_basin
visible: Head and upper torso stay above the surface while the legs remain visible through the water.
Large water area, lane strips, coping and outdoor leisure furniture stay legible.
limitations: The entry handrail still crosses the lower foreground in this near-entry view.
The existing clothed upright avatar conveys game buoyancy rather than a finished horizontal swim stroke or swimwear system.

images.name: large_open_sky_swimming_pool
visible: The normal swimming view has an unobstructed central avatar, substantial water area and clear long-axis depth.
Parasol/lounger zone and skyline establish the outdoor hotel-roof setting.
The entry rail no longer dominates the frame from this position.
limitations: Water is a simple translucent game surface with lane lines; it is not a simulated fluid or a measured hotel interior/exterior recreation.

images.name: Space_exit_back_on_deck
visible: Original avatar is fully visible and standing on the deck after the actual Space exit.
The clear strip between coping and loungers remains usable and visually open.
Loungers, side tables, parasols and the city view provide a readable leisure deck.
The roof HUD is compact and does not cover the avatar or pool exit strip.
limitations: Nearby flat neighbouring roofs remain simplified source-envelope scenery.

images.name: Space_exit_right_back_on_deck
visible: Original avatar is fully visible and standing on the opposite clear deck strip after Space exit.
Pool coping, clear walking strip, glass edge and skyline are visible without camera collapse.
No street wayfinding card or facility prop blocks the central avatar.
limitations: This opposite edge primarily looks outward over the skyline, so the leisure furniture is outside this particular view.

remaining_limits: Near-entry swimming frames include an unobstructive foreground handrail.
The arrival E prompt covers part of the lower legs while the avatar head/body and water remain clear.
Character remains the original clothed upright low-poly avatar; a complete swim animation, swimwear, fluid interaction and realistic wet materials are not established.
This reviews one representative authored pool and seven selected views, not every possible camera angle, every hotel roof or a human OS-input journey.
Source footprint/height retention and physically supported floor opening/steps/entry/exit are supported by the referenced automated test, not proven solely by screenshots.
The +1.55m game deck and sunken basin are authored accommodations above source slabs, not a claim of measured hotel roof/pool construction.
